body:
REQUIRED item fixed, and you were right in the way that stings: I wrote "a pinned checksum that lags its document is worse than no pin" and then shipped a law that lagged its enforcement. contaminationRisk appeared nowhere in the harness at af9b0d6, so the bench would have minted Calibrated for a set of five memorized stories and the only guard was a human remembering to read a document. That is the false confidence the freeze receipt exists to eliminate, manufactured by the very law meant to prevent it.

ENFORCEMENT COMMIT 4e831cb on m1/embed-bench, on top of af9b0d6 (kept separate so the protocol edit and its pin still land atomically as you required). Three files, all embed-bench: origin.scala, report.scala, LabelSuite.scala.

- FrozenManifest carries per-story contaminationRisk (typed enum Low|Medium|High) and mediumJustifications, exactly parallel to partitions as you suggested.
- Both enter the manifest digest, so risk is SET IDENTITY: a set whose risks changed is a different set with a different id. That also means a silent risk edit cannot masquerade as the same frozen set.
- FrozenSet.verify fails closed with FreezeError.NoStoryContamination when a story has no recorded risk - an old manifest cannot pass by defaulting to low.
- BenchReport.label gains two downgrade branches with typed reasons that NAME the offending stories: DiagnosticReason.ContaminatedSet (any high story in the set, Law I5 clause 3) and DiagnosticReason.UnjustifiedMedium (medium in the untouched-test partition with no written justification, clause 2). Origin.Frozen carries the set-level verdict, so the check is about the SET, not merely the stories that happen to appear in this run's cases.

MUTATION PROOF, three mutants, each applied alone and reverted:
M5 remove the high-risk downgrade branch -> LabelSuite "a high-risk story in the set downgrades a calibrated report, naming it" FAILS (expected ContaminatedSet, got calibrated).
M6 remove the fail-closed check on unrecorded risk -> "a manifest with an unrecorded risk fails closed, it does not default to low" FAILS (got Right(FrozenSet)).
M7 drop contamination from the manifest digest -> "risk is part of set identity" FAILS (identical checksums where two were expected).

EVIDENCE at 4e831cb, clean pin: embedBench 29/29 (was 25; four new I5 tests), compileAll success, scalafmtCheckAll success, scalafmtSbtCheck success. Tree clean but for the sbt shim.

SCOPE NOTE for the bead, as you asked: bd-01M14YJ8FG15S0R1ART7DTM1XZ's approved scope was the single JVM-only embedBench lazy val, and 210919f is +1676 across thirteen files. Recording explicitly that this was the BUILD ENTRY being approved rather than the extent of the work - the harness is the bead (W4 item 10 of the spike spec) - so a later reader does not read drift into it. I have put the same note on the bead itself.

LAND ORDER now: 210919f (bench bead), then af9b0d6 + 4e831cb (contamination bead). The last two are separable but should not be separated - the law and its enforcement are one change.
